# Design Document ## Overview This design fills `App.tsx`'s `Gate()` placeholder with a static, purely visual mockup of the diagram IDE's workspace shell: a top command ribbon, and a tree of resizable panes where each pane hosts one or more tabs — Hierarchy, Diagram (×2, to demonstrate multiple open documents), Property Grid, Errors & Warnings, Toolbox, and Search. Every pane briefly shows a skeleton loading shim before settling on its static placeholder content. Nothing here talks to the backend, reads a file, or implements any panel's real behavior — the deliverable is the shell's chrome and the generic pane/tab mechanism it's built from, styled entirely from the client's existing themed CSS custom properties. ## Steering Document Alignment ### Technical Standards (tech.md) * React + TypeScript, the client's established stack — no new UI framework or component library introduced. * "All styling... should be done in a centralized manner" (Frontend section): all new styles are added to the existing single `index.css`, using the existing `--color-*`/`--radius`/`--shadow` custom properties, not inline styles or a second stylesheet. * No gRPC/backend dependency of any kind, consistent with the mockup being pure client-side chrome (Requirement 1.2). ### Project Structure (structure.md) * All new components live in `src/client/src/shell/`, alongside `pages/` and `auth/` — not inside any `diagrams//client/` folder, since none of this is diagram-type-specific. * The six panel placeholders live in `shell/panels/`, one file each, per Requirement 5/6's "own component" modularity rule — each is the exact file a later spec (e.g. `project-root-folder-explorer`) will edit in place, not replace wholesale. * `hierarchy.proto`-style backend contracts are irrelevant here: this spec adds no `.proto` file and touches nothing under `src/api/` or the backend solution. ## Code Reuse Analysis ### Existing Components to Leverage * **`index.css`'s CSS custom properties** (`--color-bg`, `--color-surface`, `--color-border`, `--color-text`, `--color-text-muted`, `--color-primary`, `--color-primary-hover`, `--color-danger`, `--radius`, `--shadow`, including the `prefers-color-scheme: dark` overrides): every new class added by this spec reads these instead of hard-coding values (Requirement 7). * **`@mdi/font`** (already imported once in `main.tsx`): ribbon buttons and panel icons use `mdi mdi-*` classes exactly as `ProjectGridPage.tsx`'s trash icon already does — no new icon package. * **Existing interaction conventions**: `.primary-button:hover`'s background-shift pattern and `.field input:focus`'s focus-ring pattern are reused verbatim for ribbon buttons, tabs, and pane-resize handles (Requirement 7.3). ### Integration Points * **`App.tsx`'s `Gate()`**: the `

Workspace shell for "{openProject.name}" goes here (adp-diagram-ide).

` placeholder is replaced with ``, keeping the existing "Back to projects" button and `openProject` state exactly as they are today (Requirement 1.1/1.3). * **`adp-diagram-ide` Requirement 1**: this design is that requirement's first concrete shell implementation; later work under that spec (or `project-root-folder-explorer`, `rename-files-and-folders`, mindmap/diagram-type specs) replaces individual files under `shell/panels/` in place, never the pane/tab mechanism in `shell/` itself. ## Architecture ```mermaid graph TD Gate[App.tsx Gate] -->|openProject set| Shell[WorkspaceShellMockup] Shell --> Ribbon[RibbonBar] Shell --> Root[SplitPane root, horizontal] Root --> Left[TabbedPane: Hierarchy | Toolbox | Search] Root --> RightSplit[SplitPane, vertical] RightSplit --> Center[TabbedPane: Diagram 1 | Diagram 2] RightSplit --> Bottom[TabbedPane: Property Grid | Errors & Warnings] Left --> HierarchyPanel Left --> ToolboxPanel Left --> SearchPanel Center --> DiagramPanel Bottom --> PropertyGridPanel Bottom --> ErrorsWarningsPanel HierarchyPanel & ToolboxPanel & SearchPanel & DiagramPanel & PropertyGridPanel & ErrorsWarningsPanel --> Placeholder[PanelPlaceholder
shim to static, per panel] ``` The default arrangement (Requirement 4) is a fixed tree of two generic, content-agnostic building blocks: * **`SplitPane`**: a two-child resizable split (horizontal or vertical), draggable divider, minimum-size clamped. Composed recursively — the root horizontal split's right child is itself a vertical `SplitPane` — to build the whole layout without a dedicated "grid" component. * **`TabbedPane`**: a tab strip plus single active-content area. Takes an ordered list of `{ id, label, icon, content }` and has no knowledge of what `content` renders (Requirement 3's Modular Design principle) — a panel placeholder today, real panel content later, with no change to `TabbedPane` itself. ### Modular Design Principles * **Single file responsibility**: `SplitPane` and `TabbedPane` know nothing about panels; `RibbonBar` knows nothing about panes; each `shell/panels/*.tsx` file knows nothing about the layout tree it happens to be placed in. * **Content isolation**: a panel placeholder is handed no layout props beyond standard sizing (it fills its tab's content area) — swapping `HierarchyPanel`'s placeholder body for real content later requires no change to `WorkspaceShellMockup`'s tree definition. * **Testability**: `SplitPane`'s resize math and `TabbedPane`'s active-tab state are plain, DOM-independent enough to unit test without a full render tree. ## Components and Interfaces ### `WorkspaceShellMockup` (`shell/WorkspaceShellMockup.tsx`) * **Purpose:** Compose the ribbon and the fixed default pane tree (Requirement 4); the single integration point `App.tsx`'s `Gate()` renders. * **Interfaces:** `{ projectName: string; onBack: () => void }` — `projectName` is displayed (e.g. in a title area) but never used to fetch anything (Requirement 1.2); `onBack` is passed straight through to the existing "Back to projects" affordance already in `Gate()`. * **Dependencies:** `RibbonBar`, `SplitPane`, `TabbedPane`, the six `shell/panels/*` components. * **Reuses:** N/A — the new top-level composition root. ### `RibbonBar` (`shell/RibbonBar.tsx`) * **Purpose:** The top command ribbon (Requirement 2): a row of labeled groups of icon+label buttons. * **Interfaces:** No props — its button groups/labels are defined as a local, static data array (`[{ group: "File", buttons: [...] }, ...]`), since none of it is wired to real commands yet. * **Dependencies:** `@mdi/font` classes for icons. * **Reuses:** `.primary-button`'s hover/transition pattern, adapted to a smaller, icon-led button variant. * **Design note:** each button's `onClick` sets a purely local `pressed` visual state and contains `// TODO(diagram-ide-mockup): wire real command handler` (Requirement 2.3) — no other side effect. ### `SplitPane` (`shell/SplitPane.tsx`) * **Purpose:** A generic, resizable two-pane split, horizontal or vertical (Requirement 3.4). * **Interfaces:** `{ direction: "horizontal" | "vertical"; initialSplit: number /* 0–1 */; minSize: number /* px */; first: ReactNode; second: ReactNode }`. * **Dependencies:** None beyond React (pointer event handlers for the drag handle). * **Reuses:** `--color-border`/`--color-primary` for the divider's resting/hover state. ### `TabbedPane` (`shell/TabbedPane.tsx`) * **Purpose:** A tab strip over a single active content area (Requirement 3.1–3.3). * **Interfaces:** `{ tabs: { id: string; label: string; icon?: string; content: ReactNode }[]; defaultActiveTabId?: string }`; internal `useState` tracks the active tab, scoped to that one `TabbedPane` instance so switching one pane's tab never affects another's (Requirement 3.3). * **Dependencies:** None beyond React. * **Reuses:** `.field input:focus`'s focus-ring treatment, adapted for keyboard-focused tab buttons. ### `PanelPlaceholder` (`shell/panels/PanelPlaceholder.tsx`) * **Purpose:** The shared shim→static-placeholder presentational logic (Requirement 5, 6) every one of the six panels is built on, so that behavior isn't duplicated six times. * **Interfaces:** `{ title: string; description: string; futureSpec: string /* e.g. "project-root-folder-explorer" */ }`. Internally: mounts showing a skeleton shim, and after a short fixed `setTimeout` (Requirement 6.1) switches to the static placeholder (title + description), which renders `{/* TODO(diagram-ide-mockup): replace with 's real content */}` immediately above the placeholder markup (Requirement 5.2). * **Dependencies:** None beyond React/CSS. * **Reuses:** Requirement 7's shared theme tokens for both the shim's skeleton styling and the static placeholder's card styling. ### The six panel components (`shell/panels/{Hierarchy,Diagram,PropertyGrid,ErrorsWarnings,Toolbox,Search}Panel.tsx`) * **Purpose:** One tiny wrapper component per panel, each just calling `PanelPlaceholder` with that panel's own `title`/`description`/`futureSpec` — this is the "own component per panel" the Modular Design NFR requires, so a later spec replacing e.g. `HierarchyPanel.tsx` never touches `PanelPlaceholder` or any sibling panel. * **Interfaces:** No props (each is a fixed, named placeholder); `DiagramPanel` is instantiated twice by `WorkspaceShellMockup` with different tab labels ("Diagram 1", "Diagram 2") to satisfy Requirement 4.2, since the component itself has no notion of "which" diagram. * **Dependencies:** `PanelPlaceholder`. * **Reuses:** `PanelPlaceholder` (all six). ## Data Models This spec has no backend/proto data model. The only "data" is the local, static layout description `WorkspaceShellMockup` passes to `SplitPane`/`TabbedPane`: ```ts // shell/WorkspaceShellMockup.tsx (illustrative shape, not a persisted schema) type TabDef = { id: string; label: string; icon: string; content: ReactNode }; const leftTabs: TabDef[] = [ { id: "hierarchy", label: "Hierarchy", icon: "mdi-file-tree", content: }, { id: "toolbox", label: "Toolbox", icon: "mdi-toolbox-outline", content: }, { id: "search", label: "Search", icon: "mdi-magnify", content: }, ]; const centerTabs: TabDef[] = [ { id: "diagram-1", label: "Diagram 1", icon: "mdi-file-tree-outline", content: }, { id: "diagram-2", label: "Diagram 2", icon: "mdi-file-tree-outline", content: }, ]; const bottomTabs: TabDef[] = [ { id: "properties", label: "Property Grid", icon: "mdi-tune-variant", content: }, { id: "problems", label: "Errors & Warnings", icon: "mdi-alert-circle-outline", content: }, ]; ``` Nothing here is fetched, persisted, or shared across renders — it exists purely to parameterize the two generic layout components (Requirement 4.5's "illustrative, not prescriptive" arrangement). ## Error Handling ### Error Scenarios 1. **A pane is resized past a sensible minimum** * **Handling:** `SplitPane` clamps the drag to `minSize`, so a pane can never be dragged to zero/negative width (Requirement 3.4). * **User Impact:** The divider simply stops moving at the minimum; no error is shown because none occurred. 2. **A future developer forgets to replace a placeholder before shipping** * **Handling:** Not a runtime error — the `// TODO(diagram-ide-mockup): ...` comments (Requirement 5.2/6.3) and the visibly-a-placeholder styling (Requirement 7.5) are the guard rail, deliberately making an unreplaced placeholder obvious in both code review and the running app. * **User Impact:** N/A — this is a development-time safeguard, not a user-facing error path. No other error scenarios apply: with no network calls, no file reads, and no persisted state (Requirement 1.2, Reliability NFR), there is nothing else that can fail at runtime. ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Testing * `SplitPane`: initial split ratio, drag updates the ratio, clamping at `minSize` in both directions, both `horizontal` and `vertical` orientations. * `TabbedPane`: default active tab, clicking a tab switches content, one instance's active tab is independent of a sibling instance's (Requirement 3.3). * `PanelPlaceholder`: renders the shim first, switches to the static placeholder after the simulated delay, and never triggers a network call in either state (Requirement 1.2/6.4). ### Integration Testing * `WorkspaceShellMockup` renders the full default tree matching Requirement 4.1–4.4 exactly (which panels are tabs in which pane). * Theme: rendering under both a light and a simulated dark `prefers-color-scheme` produces the expected CSS-custom-property-driven colors, with no hard-coded color reaching the DOM (Requirement 7.1/7.2). * `App.tsx`'s `Gate()`: selecting a project renders `WorkspaceShellMockup` (not the old placeholder text), and "Back to projects" still returns to `ProjectGridPage` unchanged (Requirement 1.1/1.3). ### End-to-End Testing * Local F5 scenario: log in → open any project → the shell mockup renders with ribbon + all six panels reachable via their tabs → resize the browser window (Requirement 1.4) → drag a pane divider → switch tabs in a multi-tab pane → toggle OS-level dark mode and confirm the mockup re-themes along with the rest of the app.
